name: Roast chicken thighs and cauliflower with pickled fennel
time: About 45 minutes, most of it in the oven
intro: Bone-in thighs roasted hot until the skin crackles, cauliflower browning in the fat around them, and the month's jar spooned over everything — brine and all — so the pan juices become a sharp, bright sauce.
needs: Pickled fennel, a big forkful, plus 2 tbsp of its brine
Salt, black pepper, and chile flakes
Rice: about 1 cup cooked per serving

steps.text: Heat the oven. Pat the chicken dry and salt it on both sides.
Set the thighs skin-side up on a sheet pan, spread out, and roast them on their own.
Toss the cauliflower with the olive oil, salt, pepper, and a pinch of chile flakes.

Scatter the cauliflower around the chicken in one layer, with room between the pieces, and roast until the skin is crisp, the cauliflower is browned underneath, and the thickest thigh reads about 175°F.
Spoon the pickled fennel and its brine over the hot pan, scatter the satsuma segments, and scrape everything together with the juices. Over rice.

how_it_works: Thighs get a head start because they take longer than the cauliflower; by the time the florets go in, the pan is slick with chicken fat, and the cauliflower roasts in it. Hot oven, room on the pan, and no stirring is what browns it. The brine at the end does what a squeeze of lemon would, and the satsuma adds sweetness to the sharpness.
swaps: Fennel wedges in place of half the cauliflower.
A spoonful of melted leeks under the chicken before serving.
Grated Parmesan over the cauliflower as it comes out.
leftovers: Pack the second serving before you sit down: chicken, cauliflower, and rice, with a little more pickled fennel. Good warm or at room temperature.

sources.title: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Cauliflower and Pomegranate Pan Sauce — America's Test Kitchen
sources.note: 450°F; chicken and cauliflower on one pan, thighs to 175°F

sources.title: Sheet-Pan Chicken and Cauliflower — Food52
sources.note: thighs alone for 15 minutes, then cauliflower around them for about 15 more

sources.title: Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart — USDA
sources.note: chicken is safe at 165°F; thighs are juicier and more tender closer to 175°F

nutrition.serving: Half the recipe: two thighs, half the cauliflower, the jar, and 1 cup cooked rice.
